tasks.summary: pathContinuity now scopes its existence check to the full-history listing of commits that actually changed the selected path (ReviewSources.pathChanges, via git_path_history --full-history over the `from..to` range), filtered to descendants of `from`, instead of walking every real commit object between `from` and `to`. This is DAG-equivalent to the prior from-reachable/to-ancestor restriction (two-dot range gives ancestors-of-to; the added isAncestor(from,·) filter restores the descendants-of-from restriction the old BFS enforced via its per-edge check), and since a commit whose path entry is unchanged from its parent can only ever produce a trivially-true existence check, skipping such commits changes nothing observable while removing the O(unrelated-commits) cost. boundedProjectionSources caches pathChanges per (from,to,path) and charges one budget read per uncached listing, matching the pattern used for the other ReviewSources methods.

testCoverage.explanation: src/workflow/code-review/task-review/__tests__/projection-lineage.test.ts (new in this task) directly exercises every acceptance check: a fixed-identity fixture reproduces the exact pinned projection identity from before the change (regression on the hashed output); a dedicated test asserts pathChanges returns exactly the commits that changed a given path (verified against git-rev-parse-derived expected sets) and rejects a listing git cannot produce or a malformed-length sha as a `source` error (not `projection_limit`/`scope_conflict`); a caching test proves boundedProjectionSources serves a repeated (from,to,path) listing from cache and charges exactly one budget read for a new one; the interleaved-commits test measures that selected-path file() reads, decoded bytes and pathChanges listing calls are byte-for-byte identical whether 4 or 40 unrelated commits sit between origin and pin (walked the math above the test to confirm the fixture genuinely differs by >=36 commits, so this is not a trivial case); both side-branch deletion-kept and deletion-then-recreation merge fixtures still reject with the exact 'Unselected path disappearance or recreation interrupts lineage' message; a broken pathChanges source rejects with the injected error object itself (identity-checked), proving failures are not reclassified as a limit/conflict; and a dedicated fixture where the selected file itself changes 30 times still trips `projection_limit` under a tightened budget while fitting the production limits, confirming the optimization didn't silently raise the ceiling for genuinely large changesets. I additionally confirmed this test file's committed content at the pinned revision is identical to the current checkout (no diff) and manually traced the algebra of git's two-dot range vs. the prior from-anchored BFS to confirm the new restriction (ancestors-of-to ∩ descendants-of-from, filtered to path-changing commits) is set-equivalent to the old one, which the deletion/recreation and interleaved tests corroborate empirically. The pre-existing projection.test.ts cases (rename-chain exact-blob comparison, production budget ceilings) are unaffected by this change and still listed as passing, serving as regression coverage for the unmodified code paths pathContinuity is called from.

advice: Optional execution: I did not run the declared test commands myself — the sandbox denied shell execution permission for `npx tsx --test ...` in this session. I instead confirmed the three in-scope files (SMOKE.md, projection-lineage.test.ts, projection.ts) are byte-identical between the pinned commit 0afd7342fbde2da8a58f500cbc1f441b9a4f6a90 and the current checkout (git diff empty), so the builder-reported pass results for these exact test cases apply to the reviewed revision.

Optional improvement (non-blocking): pathContinuity calls `sources.commit(commit)` and both `sources.file(parent, path)`/`sources.file(commit, path)` for every parent of every path-changing commit, even parent edges that trivially pass; this is already far cheaper than before and the tests show it stays flat under unrelated-commit growth, so no action needed unless a future workload has very high branching factor merges that themselves repeatedly touch the path.
